text:
## Abstract
We investigated whether raw sequencing data for GEO Series GSE309890 is available for assembly. We consulted the GEO record for GSE309890, which references a BioProject with accession PRJNA1363958. We queried NCBI to find the corresponding numeric BioProject UID and then used that UID to search for SRA runs. Only one run was found (SRR1919688) belonging to Drosophila melanogaster rather than the E. coli organism described by GSE309890, indicating a mismatch between the GEO annotation and the SRA result. Moreover, no additional runs for the E. coli samples were retrieved from SRA under the listed project. Hence, there is no evidence of raw reads for GSE309890 in SRA that would enable a genome assembly. These findings highlight a gap in the official record. Researchers wishing to assemble the E. coli genome from these samples currently cannot locate raw reads in the public SRA, suggesting that the data might not be publicly released there or may be linked to a different BioProject.

## I. Introduction
### Background
GSE309890 examines E. coli transcriptomic changes under antidepressant pressure and references a BioProject accession (PRJNA1363958). Researchers commonly deposit raw sequencing reads to public archives such as SRA to facilitate further analyses like genome assembly.

### Literature Review
No literature was retrieved for this query.

### Knowledge Gap
It was unclear whether the raw sequencing data from GSE309890 were available in SRA under the referenced BioProject or any other identifier.

### Objective & Hypothesis
Objective: To determine if GSE309890 has raw sequencing runs in SRA suitable for performing an assembly of the E. coli samples.  
Hypothesis: The raw reads might be found in SRA records associated with the same BioProject, based on standard GEO-to-SRA linking practices.

## II. Materials and Methods
### Study Design
We used the GEO metadata to identify the BioProject listed and then mapped that to SRA to locate raw runs. This approach commonly surfaces raw data if it exists in public archives.

### Materials
• NCBI GEO query using “geo_series” (GSE309890)  
• NCBI’s BioProject, SRA searches using “ncbi_find_uids” and “ncbi_sra_runs_for_project”

### Procedures
1. Called "geo_series" with argument accession=GSE309890 to retrieve metadata.  
2. Queried “ncbi_find_uids” with db="bioproject" and accessions=["PRJNA1363958"].  
3. Queried “ncbi_sra_runs_for_project” with accession="1363958" (the returned UID) and max_results=100.

### Statistical Analysis
No statistical comparisons; the presence or absence of SRA runs was determined based on the result count in SRA.

## III. Results
### Data Presentation
(Table 1) Bioproject PRJNA1363958 → numeric UID → 1363958  
(Table 2) SRA runs for BioProject UID 1363958  
┌────────────┬─────────────────┬────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┐
│ UID        │ Number of runs  │ Organism reported in SRA   │ SRA Run(s)            │ Library Strategy           │
├────────────┼─────────────────┼────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤
│ 1363958    │ 1               │ Drosophila melanogaster    │ SRR1919688            │ OTHER (TRANSCRIPTOMIC)     │
└────────────┴─────────────────┴────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────┘

### Findings
• The GEO record for GSE309890 references BioProject PRJNA1363958.  
• Mapping PRJNA1363958 to a numeric ID (1363958) and searching SRA returned only one run (SRR1919688) for D. melanogaster rather than E. coli.  
• No E. coli raw reads or additional runs were discovered in the associated SRA query.  

## IV. Discussion
### Interpretation
The result indicates that GSE309890’s supposed BioProject, PRJNA1363958, does not host E. coli raw reads in SRA, but instead contains a run pertaining to D. melanogaster. This mismatch implies no accessible raw reads for E. coli from GSE309890 in SRA.

### Context
GEO often links to SRA to provide raw data for transcriptomic or genomic studies. However, this record has at least one discrepancy. It is possible the raw data, if it exists, is not yet deposited or might be under a different BioProject or accession.

### Limitations
The mismatch between the GEO record’s organism (E. coli) and the single run found for D. melanogaster in SRA suggests a potential annotation or linking error. The data may exist elsewhere or not be publicly available.

### Conclusion & Future Directions
No raw reads were identifiable for GSE309890 in SRA under the listed BioProject, so assembling E. coli genomic data from GSE309890 is currently not possible via public archives. Future steps involve contacting the data submitters or checking for updated records or alternative project links.

## References
[1] GEO record retrieval:  
NCBI GEO (geo_series) URL: https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi?db=gds&id=200309890&version=2.0  
[2] BioProject numeric UID resolution:  
NCBI E-utilities (ncbi_find_uids) URL: https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi?term=PRJNA1363958&db=bioproject  
[3] SRA runs for BioProject:  
NCBI E-utilities (ncbi_sra_runs_for_project) URL: https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/efetch.fcgi?db=sra&retmode=text  

## Acknowledgments
We acknowledge the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) for the BioProject and SRA resources, and the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) for its transcriptomic data.
